Asthma with no recent breathlessness or wheeze, no emergency visit and SpO2 94% or above. Favour walking, chair and standing strength, and breathing exercises; always warm up; stop and rest if wheezy or tight in the chest; avoid smoke, dust and cold air.
Hand exercises daily; the benefit lasts only while they continue. Move slowly; a little ache that settles within an hour is fine. Numbness or tingling in the hand: doctor first.

Exercise when it is cool, in loose cotton clothes. Afterwards wash with lukewarm water, dry well (skin folds, between the toes) and change into dry clothes; don't share towels. Eczema: put on your moisturiser after drying. Fungal infection (tinea, ringworm): keep the area dry; no cream on it unless the doctor prescribed one. If the skin is broken or oozing, do lighter exercise and tell your doctor.

Breathlessness or wheeze in the last 6 months, an emergency visit, or SpO2 below 94%: refer to a doctor.
COPD, chronic bronchitis, emphysema. Needs pulmonary rehabilitation, not a home plan of ours: refer to a doctor.

Tiredness, stiff muscles and cramps are common: start gently and build up slowly, and warm up first. Some muscle ache that settles by the next day is fine. Stop and tell your doctor about a racing heartbeat, chest pain or tingling in the hands.

A doctor writes the plan: until it is controlled, a fast or irregular heartbeat, weak muscles and weaker bones make strenuous exercise unsafe. Once controlled: walking and light strength first; weight-bearing and balance exercises help the bones.
